open_points.subject: REGISTRY_BASE_URL ownership and read timing
open_points.text: “REGISTRY_BASE_URL is read by the Registry gateway at each call” contradicts State 3’s “Environment values are read once, by runtime_settings, into RuntimeSettings; other modules read config.* constants or the settings they are handed, never the environment.” registry_gateway knows only models, while runtime_settings exclusively owns environment reading.
open_points.question: Which module owns reading REGISTRY_BASE_URL, and does registry_gateway read the process environment on every call or receive the startup value owned by runtime_settings?
options: registry_gateway directly reads REGISTRY_BASE_URL on every Registry call as an explicit exception to the State 3 configuration boundary
runtime_settings reads REGISTRY_BASE_URL once and registry_gateway uses that captured RuntimeSettings value
runtime_settings exposes a per-call configuration lookup that registry_gateway may depend on
open_points.default_guess: Treat the accepted change as controlling: registry_gateway reads REGISTRY_BASE_URL directly on every call, and State 3 must declare that exception and ownership.

witness.initial: The process starts with REGISTRY_BASE_URL pointing to Registry A; Registry A and Registry B return distinguishable project context.
events: The runtime starts and runtime_settings loads its settings.
A deployment or test harness changes the process REGISTRY_BASE_URL to Registry B.
A viewer requests the project list, causing a Registry context call.
outcomes: Following the new change, registry_gateway rereads the environment and returns context from Registry B.
Following State 3’s configuration boundary, registry_gateway uses the startup RuntimeSettings value and returns context from Registry A.
witness.observer: The viewer sees different project context or list membership, and the two Registry servers observe different requests.
